title: Observation of the Ionospheric QBO Composed by the Solar QBO and the Terrestrial QBO
content: The ionospheric quasi-biennial oscillation (QBO) is the sum of the solar QBO and the terrestrial QBO from below. In the present study, we focus on the QBO modulations of diurnal variations in mesospheric temperature and in the daily range of total electron content (ΔTEC) values at low latitudes. The diurnal tide (DW1) in mesospheric temperature is observed by the Aura Microwave Limb Sounder (Aura/MLS) from 2004 to 2021 and shows a dominant modulation at the QBO period of 28 months. This QBO modulation is transfered into the equatorial ionosphere by diurnal electric currents in the ionospheric dynamo region and the equatorial plasma fountain effect. Thus, the QBO modulation of the ΔTEC variation is partly generated by the terrestrial QBO from below. We decomposed the observed ionospheric QBO in ΔTEC from Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) into the terrestrial QBO part (from Aura/MLS) and the solar QBO part where the latter is derived from the QBO modulation of the solar flux at 10.7 cm (F10.7). The magnitude of the terrestrial QBO is 34% of the magnitude of the solar QBO in its effect on diurnal TEC variation. The supercomposition of terrestrial and solar QBO explains 81% of the ionospheric QBO signal in ΔTEC. The correlation between the QBO modulation in ΔTEC and solar flux F10.7 is 0.97. The maximal cross-correlation between the mesospheric QBO modulation in DW1 and the stratospheric QBO modulation in zonal wind is 0.97 with a certain phase lag.
